speeches.speaker: Natasha Stott Despoja
speeches.brief: The speaker, on behalf of Senators Troeth, Nettle and Carol Brown, moved to introduce a bill prohibiting misleading or deceptive advertising or notification of pregnancy counselling services. The bill was agreed to and read a first time.

speeches.speaker: Natasha Stott Despoja
speeches.brief: The Pregnancy Counselling (Truth in Advertising) Bill 2006 was introduced to prohibit misleading advertising by pregnancy counselling services and require clear disclosure of whether they provide referrals for terminations, with penalties of up to 2,000 penalty units for individuals and 10,000 for corporations. The bill also ties Commonwealth funding to compliance and annual reporting on payments and service types.

speeches.speaker: Natasha Stott Despoja
speeches.brief: The Pregnancy Counselling (Truth in Advertising) Bill 2006 requires pregnancy counselling services to disclose in advertising whether they provide referrals for terminations. The bill’s sponsors argued that current loopholes allow some services to mislead women, citing examples of deceptive advertising and the government’s $15 million pregnancy helpline.
